title: Felix and the Interior
premise: Ansel Galloway, once the conservatory's most celebrated young pianist, now cleans its halls at night, cataloguing silences instead of playing them. When the house where they grew up—kept by their late foster mother Marisol and her biological son Felix, Ansel's rival and only friend—is listed for auction, Ansel must return to claim or relinquish a past they fled at seventeen. Sorting through photographs and unsent letters, Ansel confronts the truth: Felix took the blame for the fire that ended Ansel's career, and has been in prison ever since. In the end, Ansel testifies to reopen the case, buys back the house with the conservatory's settlement money, and opens it as a rehearsal space where Felix, newly released, plays again.
about_author: Dominic Lockridge is the pen name of a former estate auctioneer who spent a decade cataloguing other people's unfinished lives. They write quietly devastating fiction about the debts families leave in attics.

chapters.title: Inventory of Unsaid Things
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Working nights as a janitor at the conservatory where they were once a prodigy, Ansel avoids the practice rooms and keeps mental lists of everything never said—to Marisol before she died, to Felix before the trial. A letter arrives: the childhood house goes to auction in six weeks. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine, the first crack in invisibility.

chapters.title: The House Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel visits the empty house and finds boxes Marisol left labeled in two hands—hers and Felix's juvenile scrawl. Among them, photographs of the three of them, and a scorched metronome from the night of the fire. The auction agent pressures Ansel to sign away any claim. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into suspicion that the official story was always wrong.

chapters.title: What Felix Carried
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, with interpolated letters from Felix read aloud in Ansel's memory. Visiting Felix in prison, Ansel learns Felix confessed to the fire to protect them—the blaze started near Ansel's lamp during a fight over Ansel's conservatory audition, and Marisol's insurance would have ruined them both. Felix refuses absolution: 'You get to be free. That's what I bought.' Emotional beat: guilt igniting into resolve; climax of confession.

chapters.title: Closing
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At the auction, Ansel bids against a developer using the conservatory's long-denied settlement for Ansel's injury, wins the house, and files a motion to vacate Felix's plea alongside a full statement. Weeks later, Felix walks out to find the front room stripped to bare floors and one piano. Emotional beat: justice outside the law, forgiveness given to the stranger in the photographs—who turns out to be themselves.
